content.comment_body: Hello everyone, I’m just starting out with PLCs. I have experience building custom controllers for aquariums and whole house automation, but am now experimenting with a [product_name] as a test platform. My goal is to monitor and control a large aquarium setup across four rooms, each with a wired LAN connection. The system involves more than 22 sensors (mainly 0-10V inputs), over 20 digital inputs, and more than 60 relay outputs. I’d like full web access to current statuses and historical sensor data (e.g., temperatures for 24 hours, 7 days, 30 days), touch controls, and comprehensive SMS alerts. Each location has its own sensors, inputs, and outlets detailed above. I’m interested in advice from experienced users about selecting the right components for this project, especially since most sensor inputs will be 0-10V signals to the PLC. Thanks in advance for sharing your expertise. [user_name]

Let me highlight some fundamental points about the current [product_name]: It can handle a max of 24 digital inputs, 20 digital outputs, 8 analog inputs, and 8 analog outputs, achievable only with expansion modules. The basic unit offers 4 analog inputs (0-10V), and if all are used, only 4 digital inputs remain. Expansion modules can add channels as needed, though analog outputs require specific expansion modules. Data logging is possible—up to 20,000 log entries per CSV, with auto file creation, and a cap of 50 files per memory card. Note that deleting files needs removal of the card to a PC, as the software can’t do it directly. SMS capability requires an additional communication module, which can only work with one PLC. Calculating the required expansion modules is a complex task specific to your needs—an overall cost calculation is necessary. Whether this system matches your requirements is up to you to judge.

You’ll encounter limitations with the [product_name] when calculating analog values. The analog inputs feature 10-bit resolution, and values are limited to 15 bits plus sign (-32768 to +32767). Basic arithmetic is supported, but if your sensors operate nonlinearly, special methods are required. When creating custom web pages, presenting decimal values is challenging since this product handles integers only, and workarounds can be complex and inefficient. Depending on your demands, you might want to consider using a [version_no] controller for more advanced processing, or stick with your custom solutions like Arduino if you’re comfortable with C++. Regards, [user_name]

[user_name], thanks for the insights. I wasn’t seeking an itemized list of modules, but was curious if the [product_name] genuinely serves as the right foundation for my use case. I was unclear whether multiple controllers could be networked together to expand the system’s input and output capacity. Appreciate your reply.

[user_name], thank you for your feedback. I’ve noticed the limitations regarding the 32k value range during my tests with 0-10V inputs. Your mention of the [version_no] controller is what I was looking for—wondering if I need a higher-end PLC to achieve my goals. Thanks again for your time!

You’ve outlined your signals and monitoring requirements (web server, touch screen, historical data), but more details are necessary. If you intend to control all aquariums, the [product_name] is adequate, and a PC running 24/7 can collect and monitor data via common industrial protocols. Crop your sensors for compatibility in terms of scaling and tolerance with analog inputs. [version_no] controllers cost more but offer better accuracy and floating-point values, supporting complex formulas for nonlinear sensors. Connection to a PC is done over industrial protocols. Review controller specifications for expansion possibilities to accommodate your requirements. If a PC isn’t planned, examine controller or display storage limitations for historical data. For deeper insight into [version_no], consider further resources. Example: Storing 100 integer values per minute requires significant memory over hourly, daily, or weekly periods, especially with floating point data. Regards, [user_name]

The situation is more complex given your nearly hundred inputs of varying types and numerous outputs, including some requiring motor controls. For a project of this magnitude, larger PLCs are advisable; the specific choice depends on your solution strategy. If rooms are nearby, a centralized system using one or two PLCs with expansion modules may suffice, and remote terminal blocks can link panels throughout different areas. This minimizes networking requirements, except for touch panels and a central computer. For distant rooms or different functions per location, a decentralized strategy—assigning dedicated PLCs per room or function—may reduce wiring needs but demands networking. Regardless, a computer and at least one HMI are essential for touch interaction. Consider SCADA software such as Fernhill SCADA for supervisory control. Good luck—your project scope is impressive!

It’s doable to expand beyond the innate limits of [product_name] by integrating MODBUS controllers for additional I/O. The downside is slower activation and input speeds on MODBUS RTU devices compared to the built-in I/O. You may hit programming space limitations; however, this can be addressed by linking multiple [product_name] units as master-to-master via LAN cables, yielding more programming capacity and allowing for greater feature complexity as needed.

analysis.insight_summary: Forum participants evaluating a large aquarium automation system with [company_name] [product_name] identify key limitations such as restricted I/O capacity, analog resolution, data storage, and the absence of integrated SMS functionality. There is discussion about cumbersome data management and limited support for nonlinear sensors, module expansion constraints, and calculation difficulties due to integer-only values. Users advise weighing the system’s capabilities against the project’s demands and consider alternatives like [version_no] controllers or decentralized architectures for larger, more complex integrations.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect the solution to efficiently scale for a high number of inputs and outputs, deliver accurate analog measurements, and facilitate robust data storage and web/HMI access. They also hope for advanced integrations such as SMS notifications and capable historical data analytics.
